content: The provided text is a detailed pharmacological interaction guide, but it is presented in a fragmented and difficult-to-read format. 1. Omaveloxolone metabolism is influenced by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration with drugs that significantly affect CYP3A4 activity. If unavoidable, reduce the omaveloxolone dose to 100 mg/day and monitor closely for adverse effects. If adverse effects occur, further reduce the dose to 50 mg/day. 2. Oxcarbazepine decreases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Netupitant is primarily metabolized by CYP3A4, so it should not be used in patients chronically taking strong CYP3A4 inducers. 3. Netupitant/palonosetron increases the levels or effects of pacritinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Monitor closely if co-administration is necessary. 4. Netupitant/palonosetron increases the levels or effects of palbociclib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely during co-administration. 5. Netupitant/palonosetron increases the levels or effects of palovarotene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with moderate CYP3A inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the palovarotene dose by 50%. 6. Paroxetine and netupitant/palonosetron increase each other's toxicity by elevating serotonin levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 7. Netupitant/palonosetron increases the levels or effects of pemigatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, reduce the pemigatinib dose as per the drug monograph. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, resume the previous pemigatinib dose. 8. Pentobarbital decreases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 9. Phenobarbital decreases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 10. Phenytoin decreases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 11. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. No dosage adjustment is required. 12. Primidone decreases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 13. Protriptyline and netupitant/palonosetron increase each other's toxicity by elevating serotonin levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 14. Quinidine increases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. No dosage adjustment is required. 15. Rasagiline and netupitant/palonosetron increase each other's toxicity by elevating serotonin levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 16. Netupitant/palonosetron increases the levels or effects of repotrectinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Discontinue strong or moderate CYP3A inhibitors and wait 3–5 elimination half-lives before initiating repotrectinib. 17. Ribociclib increases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 19. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 20. Rifapentine decreases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 21. Netupitant/palonosetron increases the levels or effects of rimegepant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid repeating the rimegepant dose within 48 hours if co-administered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. 22. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. No dosage adjustment is required. 23. Rizatriptan and netupitant/palonosetron increase each other's toxicity by elevating serotonin levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 24. Rucaparib increases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the dosage of CYP3A4 substrates if clinically indicated and monitor closely. 25. Netupitant/palonosetron increases the levels or effects of seladelpar by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution in patients who are poor CYP2C9 metabolizers and are co-administered a moderate/strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 26. Selegiline and netupitant/palonosetron increase each other's toxicity by elevating serotonin levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 27. Selegiline transdermal and netupitant/palonosetron increase each other's toxicity by elevating serotonin levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 28. Netupitant/palonosetron increases the levels or effects of selumetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the selumetinib dosage as per the drug monograph. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, resume the previous selumetinib dose. 29. Sertraline and netupitant/palonosetron increase each other's toxicity by elevating serotonin levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 30. Netupitant/palonosetron increases the levels or effects of siponimod by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration of siponimod with a moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitor plus a moderate or strong CYP2C9 inhibitor is not recommended. 31. Netupitant/palonosetron increases the levels or effects of sonidegib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. If unavoidable, administer the moderate CYP3A inhibitor for less than 14 days and monitor closely for adverse reactions, particularly musculoskeletal adverse reactions. 32. Netupitant/palonosetron increases the levels or effects of sparsentan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. No dosage adjustment is needed. Monitor blood pressure, serum potassium, edema, and kidney function regularly if sparsentan is co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 33. St. John’s Wort decreases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 34. Stiripentol affects CYP3A4 metabolism as both an inhibitor and inducer. Monitor CYP3A4 substrates co-administered with stiripentol for increased or decreased effects. Dosage adjustments may be required. 35. Netupitant/palonosetron increases the levels or effects of sufentanil SL by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase sufentanil plasma concentration, leading to prolonged or severe adverse effects, including potentially fatal respiratory depression. 36. Sumatriptan and netupitant/palonosetron increase each other's toxicity by elevating serotonin levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 37. Sumatriptan intranasal and netupitant/palonosetron increase each other's toxicity by elevating serotonin levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 38. Tazemetostat decreases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 39. Tecovirimat is a weak CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor sensitive CYP3A4 substrates for effectiveness if co-administered. 40. Netupitant/palonosetron increases the levels or effects of tezacaftor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the tezacaftor dosage regimen if co-administered with a moderate CYP3A inhibitor. 41. Netupitant/palonosetron increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. No dosage adjustment is required. 43. Netupitant/palonosetron increases the levels or effects of trabectedin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Tranylcypromine and netupitant/palonosetron increase each other's toxicity by elevating serotonin levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 45. Trimipramine and netupitant/palonosetron increase each other's toxicity by elevating serotonin levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 46. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid concomitant use with CYP3A substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious or life-threatening toxicities. If unavoidable, reduce the CYP3A substrate dose according to product labeling. 47. Netupitant/palonosetron increases the levels or effects of vardenafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Vardenafil dosage may need to be reduced if co-administered with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 48. Netupitant/palonosetron increases the levels or effects of venetoclax by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If a moderate CYP3A inhibitor must be used, reduce the venetoclax dose by at least 50%. Monitor closely for signs of venetoclax toxicities. 49. Venlafaxine and netupitant/palonosetron increase each other's toxicity by elevating serotonin levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 50. Netupitant/palonosetron increases the levels or effects of voclosporin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 51. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. No dosage adjustment is required. 52. Netupitant/palonosetron increases the levels or effects of zanubrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce zanubrutinib (a CYP3A4 substrate) to 80 mg PO BID when co-administered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. Interrupt the dose as recommended for adverse reactions. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor, resume the previous dose of zanubrutinib. 53. Zolmitriptan and netupitant/palonosetron increase each other's toxicity by elevating serotonin levels. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug.
